findings.title: Every failure is reported as "could not reach that environment"; decision call has no stale-credential retry
findings.body:
`Effect.mapError` at the end of `Effect.fn` wraps every error (timeout, schema decode failure, relay rejection, network) in `ConnectMcpApprovalUnavailableError`. `ApproveAgentSurface.tsx:45` therefore always shows that class's message, and its "Could not reach this environment. Try again." fallback at line 47 is dead.

The `approval` call retries a stale credential through `isUnauthorizedResponse` (line 96). The `decision` call (line 99) has no equivalent. On the server, `approvingSession` swallows auth errors into `undefined` (`McpOAuth.ts:421`). `approve` then fails with "Your session cannot approve this request. Enter a pairing code instead." (`McpOAuth.ts:477`), and that text reaches the user as a `refused` answer.

The csrf token is bound to the session id (`McpOAuth.ts:310-319`). If the Connect token is renewed between loading the consent screen and pressing Approve, the token from `approval` no longer matches the session `decision` authenticates with. I did not verify whether a renewed Connect token maps to a new environment session id. If it does, retrying Approve fails the same way until the page is reloaded. The footer link to the sign-in code page is the only way out.

Suggest mapping only reach/auth failures to the unavailable error. If rotation does change the session id, reload the details and csrf token on a refused decision.

findings.title: Second config for the same env var, with a different default than `hostedAppUrlConfig`
findings.body: `agentApprovalAppUrlConfig` reads `T3CODE_HOSTED_APP_URL`, the same variable as `hostedAppUrlConfig` (line 113). It differs only in defaulting to the nightly URL on nightly builds. `hostedAppUrlConfig` still defaults to app.t3.codes on nightly and is still used for CLI auth (`CliTokenManager.ts:514`) and for MCP thread links (`McpOAuth.ts:590`). One server build now resolves two different hosted apps from one variable. If nightly should use the nightly hosted app, put the nightly default in `hostedAppUrlConfig`. If not, say why only agent approval needs it.

findings.title: New hosted-approval client path has no tests; the removed tests covered the old path only
findings.body: This PR deletes `peerPairingCode.test.ts` and `connectAgentApproval.test.ts`, which covered the old code-minting path. Nothing covers the replacement `callConnectMcpApproval`: the `redirectTo` vs details mapping in `answerFrom`, `AuthMcpApprovalError` becoming `refused`, the `csrfToken === undefined` retry, and the `Unavailable` mapping. The server test does cover the bearer approve path and the redirect to the hosted app. AGENTS.md asks for tests on auth and protocol logic; one case with a stubbed `RemoteEnvironmentAuthorization` and fetch (like the deleted harness) would cover the client side.

findings.title: Wizard drops the code whenever the capability is present, but the hosted redirect is conditional
findings.body: `hostedApproval` is read from the static `mcpHostedApproval` capability (ServerEnvironment.ts:292, always true). The server only redirects /authorize to the hosted page when the link is linked, not revoked, and `tunnelHostname` matches the issuer host, and never for peer-link clients (mcpOAuthHttp.ts:78-93, 129-133). In every other case the agent lands on `/connect-agent`, which needs a code or a browser session. The wizard then no longer offers a code and says to approve with a T3 Connect account (line 569). Is there a case where the gate is `open` but the hosted redirect is not taken, such as a link revoked after the reachability check? If so, the user has no code to paste from the wizard and has to go to Settings → Sharing & access.

contracts.action: authorize on the T3 Connect tunnel host now redirects to the hosted app's /approve-agent with environment=<id> instead of the environment's own /connect-agent page
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous path redirected every valid authorize request to /connect-agent and returned `connectSignIn` in the approval details so the page could hop to the hosted app and bring back a minted code.
contracts.before_after: Before: environment page loaded, then optionally handed off to hosted app, code returned in fragment. After: server redirects straight to the hosted app only when the link is live and the tunnel hostname matches the issuer host; peer links and other hosts stay on /connect-agent. Lookup failures fall back to the local page (orElseSucceed none).
contracts.visible_effect: Owner lands on app.t3.codes (or nightly.app.t3.codes on nightly builds), signs in to Connect and approves with no code.
contracts.failure_mode: If the hosted app lacks the new page (deploy ordering) the redirect goes to a page that cannot approve. There is no fallback because the redirect is unconditional on server state. The `mcpHostedApproval` capability is only consumed by the UI dialog.

contracts.action: approval/decision endpoints now authenticate any session via authenticateHttpRequest (cookie, bearer or DPoP) instead of browser cookie only
contracts.equivalent_path: The old `authenticateBrowserSession` required a browser cookie credential and method browser-session-cookie.
contracts.before_after: Before: only a browser cookie session could one-click approve. After: any non-MCP-client session holding access:write and orchestration:read can. The scope-subset check at line 475 is unchanged, and the csrf token is still bound to session id and authorization. `authenticateToken` rejects MCP-client audience tokens. CloudLink-issued Connect sessions carry AuthStandardClientScopes, which include access:write.
contracts.visible_effect: Owner approving from the hosted app via Connect sees one-click levels and can approve. The same bearer holders could already mint pairing credentials with these scopes, so this does not widen their authority.
contracts.failure_mode: Auth errors are swallowed into `undefined`, so a stale or invalid credential looks like "session cannot approve" rather than an auth error (see finding on decision retry).

contracts.action: Hosted ApproveAgentSurface loads details and posts decisions over Connect via DPoP
contracts.equivalent_path: ConnectAgentSurface's primaryTransport, which uses the cookie and runPrimaryHttp.
contracts.before_after: Before: the page minted a code and navigated back with the code in the URL fragment. After: it renders the shared McpConsent with a Connect transport and the page itself follows the redirectTo returned by the environment. `agentRedirectUrl` restricts the target to https or loopback http.
contracts.visible_effect: Consent screen on the hosted app. Unreachable or wrong-account environments show "Could not reach that environment through T3 Connect with this account.". The footer offers "Use another account" and, once the environment URL is known, a sign-in-code link.
contracts.failure_mode: `authorizeDpopHttp` is called once outside the 10 s request timeout and again inside it. The service bounds its own token exchange with DPOP_AUTHORIZATION_TIMEOUT_MS, so the first call is not unbounded. The inner request loop is bounded by the 10 s `timeoutOrElse`. A timeout shows the generic unavailable message and the user can click again. If the environment is unreachable, the code-instead link never appears because `environment` is only set after a successful call.

contracts.action: OptionalBearerHeaders added to mcpOAuth approval and decision endpoints
contracts.equivalent_path: Other environment HTTP endpoints that accept optional authorization/dpop headers.
contracts.before_after: Before: the endpoints had no headers schema, so the hosted app could not send credentials through the typed client. After: callers must pass `headers`. All callers were updated: PeerLinks.ts passes `{}`, ConnectAgentSurface passes `{}`, and the connect client passes the DPoP headers.
contracts.failure_mode: A caller outside the repo that compiles against the contract needs `headers: {}`.

contracts.action: Agent sign-in page follows server-supplied redirects through an https/loopback-http allowlist
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous submitDecision/load called window.location.replace(answer.url) with no check.
contracts.before_after: Before, any redirectTo string was followed. Now `agentRedirectUrl` accepts only https, or http on localhost/127.0.0.1/[::1]. The server registration check (McpOAuth.ts:110-111, LOOPBACK_HOSTNAMES at line 60) accepts the same set, and `isLoopbackHost` also accepts these three hosts, so legitimate agent redirects are unaffected.
contracts.visible_effect: A refused redirect shows 'The environment returned an address this page will not open.' in the invalid screen (load) or the error alert (decide).
contracts.failure_mode: On the decide path a refused redirect leaves pending cleared and the error shown, though the server has already consumed the code and issued the authorization. This is only reachable if the server returned a disallowed URL, which it validates at registration.

contracts.action: Approve button is disabled for 700ms after the page shows and after every window focus or visibility change
contracts.equivalent_path: No earlier equivalent. Approve was enabled as soon as a decision could be built.
contracts.before_after: `armed` starts false, is set by a timer once `loaded.status` is ready, and `rearm` resets it on `focus` and `visibilitychange`. The effect cleanup clears the timer and listeners. `canApprove` and the form submit both check `canApprove`, so Enter in the code field is gated too. Deny is not gated.
contracts.visible_effect: Approve is briefly disabled after load and after returning to the tab, so a click aimed at another window cannot land on it.
contracts.failure_mode: No failure found. The state is local and is rebuilt on remount because loaded starts as loading.

contracts.action: Create-agent wizard skips the Access step and the code when the environment advertises mcpHostedApproval
contracts.equivalent_path: Old path: the Access step, then ApprovalCode via mintMcpApprovalCodeOn. Hosted path: the agent's authorize request redirects to /approve-agent (mcpOAuthHttp.ts:129-133), which uses McpConsent with requireLevelChoice and the owner's T3 Connect session.
contracts.before_after: Step indices stay 0 to 2 internally. The shown step is mapped to 1 when hosted and step 2, and a click on step index 1 jumps to 2. Next from step 0 goes to 2. `ConnectStep` receives access=null, so it shows the explanatory text instead of ApprovalCode, and `LinkedLine` shows each link's own level. The mapping is consistent with the 2-entry steps array.
contracts.visible_effect: Two-step wizard. The Connect step tells the user to choose a level and approve with their T3 Connect account.
contracts.failure_mode: The hosted redirect is conditional on link state (mcpOAuthHttp.ts:81) and on the client not being a peer link, while the wizard keys only on the static capability. See the finding at line 125.
contracts.open_question: Can the wizard gate be open while the server's hostedApprovalUrl returns none, other than for peer-link clients?

summary:
**Batch 1 of 2.** The change moves T3 Connect agent sign-in approval from a minted-code round trip to approving on the hosted app with the owner's Connect session. I found no blocker. The server accepts any non-MCP-client session holding access:write and orchestration:read, which does not widen authority since Connect sessions already carry those scopes. Three smaller points: all Connect call failures are collapsed into one \"unavailable\" message and the decision call has no stale-credential retry (an open question whether a renewed token rotates the session id and breaks the csrf token); `agentApprovalAppUrlConfig` is a second config for the same env var with a different default; and the new client path has no tests after the old ones were deleted.

**Batch 2 of 2.** I found nothing that needs fixing in this part. The redirect allowlist matches the server's registration check, the 700ms arm delay is self-contained, and the doc text matches the server behavior I read. One low-confidence consider is attached to the wizard's reliance on the always-true `mcpHostedApproval` capability. The server only redirects to the hosted page when the link is live, the tunnel host matches and the client is not a peer link. Outside this part, `apps/web/src/components/sidebar/mainAppLocation.ts:18` lists `/connect-agent` as a shell-less path but not `/approve-agent`, so the new consent page can be recorded as the page to return to.
